template_record.description: Decommission a server from use including removal from backup, systems management and monitoring systems and disposal of hardware
template_record.implementation_plan: --Inform local IT of the necessary steps to change DHCP and static IP clients to use a different DC/DNS servers for name resolution--Use Network Monitor to check if any DNS queries are being received by the DC before demoting, reconfigure any requestors DNS before continuing--Notify the Operations Teams about the demotion via email--Place the DC in outage mode in monitoring tools--Run the AD DC Demotion Preparation tool in management tools--Logon to the DC to be removed from Active Directory--Run DCPROMO to uninstall AD and reboot--Uninstall DNS--Remove the server from the domain by joining it to a workgroup and reboot--Logon to a regional hub DC in the same domain as the DC that was removed--Delete the computer object--Delete any leftover DNS records--Locate the DNS zone for the domain and then right-click it and select properties--Click the name servers tab--Locate and delete the entry for the removed DNS server (if present)--Delete the server object in AD Sites and Services--Logon to a forest root DC--launch the DNS console on the forest root DC--locate and delete all DNS records that point to the removed DC in the _msdcs zone and in any child zones of it --Also verify that no record exists in the delegated zone for the child domain zone--Create requests to remove device from anti-virus, endpoint management, monitoring and ServiceNow CMDB

std_change_producer_version.display_value: Decommission local office Domain Controller - 1

template_record.description: Decommission a server from use including removal from backup, systems management and monitoring systems and disposal of hardware
template_record.implementation_plan: --Inform local IT of the necessary steps to change DHCP and static IP clients to use a different DC/DNS servers for name resolution--Use Network Monitor to check if any DNS queries are being received by the DC before demoting, reconfigure any requestors DNS before continuing--Notify the Operations Teams about the demotion via email--Place the DC in outage mode in monitoring tools--Run the AD DC Demotion Preparation tool in management tools--Logon to the DC to be removed from Active Directory--Run DCPROMO to uninstall AD and reboot--Uninstall DNS--Remove the server from the domain by joining it to a workgroup and reboot--Logon to a regional hub DC in the same domain as the DC that was removed--Delete the computer object--Delete any leftover DNS records--Locate the DNS zone for the domain and then right-click it and select properties--Click the name servers tab--Locate and delete the entry for the removed DNS server (if present)--Delete the server object in AD Sites and Services--Logon to a forest root DC--launch the DNS console on the forest root DC--locate and delete all DNS records that point to the removed DC in the _msdcs zone and in any child zones of it --Also verify that no record exists in the delegated zone for the child domain zone--Create requests to remove device from anti-virus, endpoint management, monitoring and ServiceNow CMDB

template_record.description: Decommission a server from use including removal from backup, systems management and monitoring systems and disposal of hardware
template_record.implementation_plan: --Inform local IT of the necessary steps to change DHCP and static IP clients to use a different DC/DNS servers for name resolution--Use Network Monitor to check if any DNS queries are being received by the DC before demoting, reconfigure any requestors DNS before continuing--Notify the Operations Teams about the demotion via email--Place the DC in outage mode in monitoring tools--Run the AD DC Demotion Preparation tool in management tools--Logon to the DC to be removed from Active Directory--Run DCPROMO to uninstall AD and reboot--Uninstall DNS--Remove the server from the domain by joining it to a workgroup and reboot--Logon to a regional hub DC in the same domain as the DC that was removed--Delete the computer object--Delete any leftover DNS records--Locate the DNS zone for the domain and then right-click it and select properties--Click the name servers tab--Locate and delete the entry for the removed DNS server (if present)--Delete the server object in AD Sites and Services--Logon to a forest root DC--launch the DNS console on the forest root DC--locate and delete all DNS records that point to the removed DC in the _msdcs zone and in any child zones of it --Also verify that no record exists in the delegated zone for the child domain zone--Create requests to remove device from anti-virus, endpoint management, monitoring and ServiceNow CMDB

template_record.description: Decommission a server from use including removal from backup, systems management and monitoring systems and disposal of hardware
template_record.implementation_plan: --Inform local IT of the necessary steps to change DHCP and static IP clients to use a different DC/DNS servers for name resolution--Use Network Monitor to check if any DNS queries are being received by the DC before demoting, reconfigure any requestors DNS before continuing--Notify the Operations Teams about the demotion via email--Place the DC in outage mode in monitoring tools--Run the AD DC Demotion Preparation tool in management tools--Logon to the DC to be removed from Active Directory--Run DCPROMO to uninstall AD and reboot--Uninstall DNS--Remove the server from the domain by joining it to a workgroup and reboot--Logon to a regional hub DC in the same domain as the DC that was removed--Delete the computer object--Delete any leftover DNS records--Locate the DNS zone for the domain and then right-click it and select properties--Click the name servers tab--Locate and delete the entry for the removed DNS server (if present)--Delete the server object in AD Sites and Services--Logon to a forest root DC--launch the DNS console on the forest root DC--locate and delete all DNS records that point to the removed DC in the _msdcs zone and in any child zones of it --Also verify that no record exists in the delegated zone for the child domain zone--Create requests to remove device from anti-virus, endpoint management, monitoring and ServiceNow CMDB

template_record.backout_plan: Due to the nature of this procedure any means to back out of this after the process has begun should not be implemented. template_record.description: Decommission a server from use including removal from backup, systems management and monitoring systems and disposal of hardware
template_record.implementation_plan: --Inform local IT of the necessary steps to change DHCP and static IP clients to use a different DC/DNS servers for name resolution--Use Network Monitor to check if any DNS queries are being received by the DC before demoting, reconfigure any requestors DNS before continuing--Notify the Operations Teams about the demotion via email--Place the DC in outage mode in monitoring tools--Run the AD DC Demotion Preparation tool in management tools--Logon to the DC to be removed from Active Directory--Run DCPROMO to uninstall AD and reboot--Uninstall DNS--Remove the server from the domain by joining it to a workgroup and reboot--Logon to a regional hub DC in the same domain as the DC that was removed--Delete the computer object--Delete any leftover DNS records--Locate the DNS zone for the domain and then right-click it and select properties--Click the name servers tab--Locate and delete the entry for the removed DNS server (if present)--Delete the server object in AD Sites and Services--Logon to a forest root DC--launch the DNS console on the forest root DC--locate and delete all DNS records that point to the removed DC in the _msdcs zone and in any child zones of it --Also verify that no record exists in the delegated zone for the child domain zone--Create requests to remove device from anti-virus, endpoint management, monitoring and ServiceNow CMDB

std_change_producer_version.display_value: Decommission local office Domain Controller - 1

template_record.description: Decommission a server from use including removal from backup, systems management and monitoring systems and disposal of hardware
template_record.implementation_plan: --Inform local IT of the necessary steps to change DHCP and static IP clients to use a different DC/DNS servers for name resolution--Use Network Monitor to check if any DNS queries are being received by the DC before demoting, reconfigure any requestors DNS before continuing--Notify the Operations Teams about the demotion via email--Place the DC in outage mode in monitoring tools--Run the AD DC Demotion Preparation tool in management tools--Logon to the DC to be removed from Active Directory--Run DCPROMO to uninstall AD and reboot--Uninstall DNS--Remove the server from the domain by joining it to a workgroup and reboot--Logon to a regional hub DC in the same domain as the DC that was removed--Delete the computer object--Delete any leftover DNS records--Locate the DNS zone for the domain and then right-click it and select properties--Click the name servers tab--Locate and delete the entry for the removed DNS server (if present)--Delete the server object in AD Sites and Services--Logon to a forest root DC--launch the DNS console on the forest root DC--locate and delete all DNS records that point to the removed DC in the _msdcs zone and in any child zones of it --Also verify that no record exists in the delegated zone for the child domain zone--Create requests to remove device from anti-virus, endpoint management, monitoring and ServiceNow CMDB

template_record.description: Decommission a server from use including removal from backup, systems management and monitoring systems and disposal of hardware
template_record.implementation_plan: --Inform local IT of the necessary steps to change DHCP and static IP clients to use a different DC/DNS servers for name resolution--Use Network Monitor to check if any DNS queries are being received by the DC before demoting, reconfigure any requestors DNS before continuing--Notify the Operations Teams about the demotion via email--Place the DC in outage mode in monitoring tools--Run the AD DC Demotion Preparation tool in management tools--Logon to the DC to be removed from Active Directory--Run DCPROMO to uninstall AD and reboot--Uninstall DNS--Remove the server from the domain by joining it to a workgroup and reboot--Logon to a regional hub DC in the same domain as the DC that was removed--Delete the computer object--Delete any leftover DNS records--Locate the DNS zone for the domain and then right-click it and select properties--Click the name servers tab--Locate and delete the entry for the removed DNS server (if present)--Delete the server object in AD Sites and Services--Logon to a forest root DC--launch the DNS console on the forest root DC--locate and delete all DNS records that point to the removed DC in the _msdcs zone and in any child zones of it --Also verify that no record exists in the delegated zone for the child domain zone--Create requests to remove device from anti-virus, endpoint management, monitoring and ServiceNow CMDB

template_record.description: Decommission a server from use including removal from backup, systems management and monitoring systems and disposal of hardware
template_record.implementation_plan: --Inform local IT of the necessary steps to change DHCP and static IP clients to use a different DC/DNS servers for name resolution--Use Network Monitor to check if any DNS queries are being received by the DC before demoting, reconfigure any requestors DNS before continuing--Notify the Operations Teams about the demotion via email--Place the DC in outage mode in monitoring tools--Run the AD DC Demotion Preparation tool in management tools--Logon to the DC to be removed from Active Directory--Run DCPROMO to uninstall AD and reboot--Uninstall DNS--Remove the server from the domain by joining it to a workgroup and reboot--Logon to a regional hub DC in the same domain as the DC that was removed--Delete the computer object--Delete any leftover DNS records--Locate the DNS zone for the domain and then right-click it and select properties--Click the name servers tab--Locate and delete the entry for the removed DNS server (if present)--Delete the server object in AD Sites and Services--Logon to a forest root DC--launch the DNS console on the forest root DC--locate and delete all DNS records that point to the removed DC in the _msdcs zone and in any child zones of it --Also verify that no record exists in the delegated zone for the child domain zone--Create requests to remove device from anti-virus, endpoint management, monitoring and ServiceNow CMDB

std_change_producer_version.display_value: Decommission local office Domain Controller - 1

template_record.description: Resend the complete BGP table to neighboring routers--Both neighbors need to support soft reset route refresh capability.--Stores complete BGP table of you neighbor in router memory.--Not a good idea on a peering router with full feed, due to the memory requirements.
template_record.implementation_plan: -- Place router into maintenance mode in the monitoring platform-- Logon to router through SSH-- Run the following commandrouter(config-router)#router bgp 12345router(config-router)#neighbor {neighbor ip} soft-reconfig [inbound]router#clear ip bgp {neighbor ip} soft in-- Confirm the sessions have been cleared-- Place router back into operational mode in the monitoring platform
